note: Series of articles, read by tools/build_articles.py. Each series lists its parts in reading order (slug = the file name in articles/src without .md, label = the short name shown in the series box). Optional featured: YYYY-MM-DD makes the whole series the Featured line from that date, by the same rule as an article's featured: line (the newest date that has arrived wins; a series wins a tie). Optional picture: a tile id with an optional range and ov ("health_jobs range=10y"), the picture on the Featured card while the series is featured. Optional teaser (Nov 9): the few words after the title on the home page's one-line Featured strip, lower case, no closing period.

health-care.title: Health care: what it costs, who gains, who lobbies
health-care.dek: Three pages, read in order: what coverage costs and who pays for it, who comes out ahead and behind under each way of changing it, and who lobbies Washington over it.

electric-vehicles.title: Electric vehicles: the case, and the claims
electric-vehicles.dek: Two pages, read in order: what an electric car costs to buy, fuel and own against a gas car, and where charging stands; then fifteen repeated claims about EVs, from both directions, checked against the evidence.

news-ownership.title: Who owns the news: a century, and this year
news-ownership.dek: Two pages, read in order: how ownership of American news and the money that paid for it changed from 1919 to the 2020s, and what changed in 2026, from the end of the national ownership cap to CNN and CBS News under one owner and the rules on foreign money.

parts.label: A century of who owned it

main-street.title: Who Owns Main Street
main-street.dek: Nine pages, read in order: how private equity and corporate groups bought vet clinics, dental offices and eye practices, usually keeping the local name; why pharmacies changed hands differently; who owns the plumbing, heating and electrical companies and who makes the equipment they install; who owns the farms, and the few companies that sell farmers their seed and fertilizer and buy what they raise; who owns the houses that are rented out, and what a 2026 law bars the largest owners from buying; and where the money from all of it goes.

property-tax.title: Property taxes: how the rate gets set, and how states limit it
property-tax.dek: Two pages, read in order: how a local government's budget, the value of its property and the rollback rate produce a tax rate, worked through for one made-up town; then the three ways states limit property taxes, and what changed in 2026.

debt.title: Debt: four kinds of borrower, and why Washington isn't a household
debt.dek: Two pages, read in order: how borrowing works for a household, a city, a state and the federal government, and which of them has to cut back when a recession hits; then the four ways the family-budget comparison fails for Washington, and why a business that never closes is the better one.

money-traps.title: Money Traps
money-traps.dek: Twenty-one short pages on the ways money leaks out of a household, especially a new one, from overdraft fees and card minimums to car loans, scams, gig taxes, co-signing and student debt: how each trap works, what it costs in dollars, how to avoid it, and the policy fight around it.
money-traps.teaser: short pages on how money leaks out of a household
